title: Day Trading Strategies
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/0/body: The **opening range** is the high and low of price in the **first stretch after a session opens**, like the first 30 minutes of London or New York. In the **ORB strategy**, a break above its high is a buy signal and a break below its low is a sell signal.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/1/body: Enter on a **candle close outside the range**, not just a wick. The stop loss usually goes at **mid-range** or **the other side of the range**, and the target is **1 to 2 times the range height**.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/2/prompt: The first two candles made the 30-minute opening range. Tap the candle that gave the ORB buy signal.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/2/explan: The 5th candle only poked above the range high with its wick and closed back inside, so that wasn't a signal. This candle is the first whose body closed above 1.2725, so this is the ORB signal.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/3/prompt: The opening range ran from 1.2700 to 1.2725 and price broke to the upside. Where's the “1× range height” target, measured from the range high?
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/3/explan: Range height: 1.2725 − 1.2700 = 25 pips. Add 25 pips to the range high and you get 1.2750. That's a common target, not a guaranteed move.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/4/statem: In ORB, a wick poking above the range high is enough to enter.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/4/explan: A wick means price wasn't accepted up there and came back. ORB waits for a candle body to close outside the range, so you get caught in fewer fakeouts.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/5/prompt: You bought the break of the range high. Using the “stop at mid-range” rule, which line is your stop loss?
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/5/explan: Line A sits exactly halfway between the high (1.0870) and the low (1.0850), at 1.0860. Line B is below the range low; that's the riskier “other side of the range” option. A stop right on the range high gets hit by the smallest pullback.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/6/prompt: Gold's first 30-minute range was between 2395 and 2402, and the last candle closed below the range low with a long body. What's the ORB trade?
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/6/explan: A strong body closing below the opening range low is an ORB sell signal and shows sellers have taken control. Further downside is more likely. Put the stop loss at mid-range or above the range, and aim for about 1× the range height.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/7/prompt: Put the steps of the ORB strategy in order.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/7/items/: Mark the high and low of the first 30 minutes
Wait for a candle to close outside the range
Enter and put your stop loss at mid-range
Exit at 1 to 2 times the range height
lessons/day-trading-u2-l1/steps/7/explan: The range has to finish first so its high and low are known. After that, only a close outside the range counts as a signal, and both the stop loss and the target come from the range itself.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/0/body: **VWAP (volume-weighted average price)** is an average price where each trade counts as much as its **volume**, calculated from the **start of the day or session**. Many institutions use it as a benchmark for today's “fair” price.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/1/body: Price **above VWAP** means buyers have the upper hand today, so a day trader mostly looks to **buy pullbacks to VWAP**. **Below VWAP**, it's the opposite. VWAP starts **fresh** every day.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/1/tip: Here VWAP is drawn as a simple flat line. On a real platform it's a curve that gets smoother as the day goes on.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/2/prompt: Where is price relative to VWAP, and who has the upper hand today?
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/2/explan: Every candle is below VWAP, and the highs and lows keep stepping lower. So most of today's buyers are underwater versus the average price, and sellers have the upper hand.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/3/prompt: Two batches of ETH traded today: 1 unit at 3,000 and 3 units at 3,030. What's the VWAP?
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/3/explan: (3,000 × 1 + 3,030 × 3) ÷ 4 = 12,090 ÷ 4 = 3,022.5. A simple average would be 3,015, but VWAP gets pulled toward the price with more volume.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/4/prompt: Bitcoin has been above VWAP since the morning and just pulled back to it. Tap the buy trigger candle.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/4/explan: Price reached VWAP with a red candle and dipped slightly below it, but the next candle pushed back up with a long green body. That candle confirms buyers defended VWAP. Put the stop loss below the pullback low.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/5/statem: Spot forex has no centralized volume, so VWAP there is calculated from the broker's tick volume.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/5/explan: Spot forex is an over-the-counter market, so total market volume isn't available. That makes forex VWAP an approximation. In stocks, futures and crypto, the volume is more real.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/6/prompt: Price has been below VWAP all day, and the last candle rallied up to VWAP but got rejected. What's the next trade?
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/6/explan: On a day when sellers have the upper hand, VWAP acts like resistance. The upper wick and the close below VWAP show buyers couldn't hold price up there. A sell is more likely, with a stop loss above the wick.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/7/prompt: Price has been above VWAP since the morning, but now two strong candles in a row have closed below it. What's the sensible read?
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/7/option: Buyers' edge has weakened; skip new buys for now
Nothing has changed; keep buying like before
VWAP is only for stocks, so it doesn't matter
Remove the stop losses on your open buys
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/7/explan: Holding below VWAP means today's average trader is no longer in profit, and the day's direction may have flipped. A day trader holds off on new buys here.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/8/senten: VWAP is an average price weighted by ___ that resets every ___.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l2/steps/8/explan: Prices with more volume count for more, and the calculation resets at the start of each day or session.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/title: The London and New York Sessions
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/0/body: Forex runs 24 hours, but activity isn't even. The **London session** runs about 08:00 to 17:00 London time and the **New York session** about 08:00 to 17:00 New York time. Their **overlap**, the first few hours of New York, is usually the most liquid part of the day.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/0/tip: The US and the UK start daylight saving time on different dates, so these hours are approximate.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/1/title: How each session tends to behave
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/1/body: Many traders notice that **Asia** is quieter for European pairs, **London** often starts the day's main move, and **New York**, with US news (usually 8:30 New York time), can **extend or reverse** that move. After the overlap, volatility usually fades.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/2/prompt: Put these parts of the trading day in time order (London time).
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/2/explan: The forex day starts with Asia, London opens around 08:00, New York joins around 13:00, and the day ends with the New York close (around 22:00 London time).
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/3/prompt: Roughly what hours is the London–New York overlap, in London time?
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/3/explan: New York opens around 08:00 local time, which is usually 13:00 in London, and London closes around 17:00. So the overlap is roughly 13:00 to 17:00 London time.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/4/prompt: This 1-hour chart starts at midnight London time. Tap the candle most likely to show the London open.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/4/explan: If the first candle is 00:00, the 9th candle is 08:00 London time, right where candles suddenly get bigger and volume multiplies. The chart confirms it.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/5/statem: Because of daylight saving time, session open times in your local time can shift by about an hour during the year.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/5/explan: London and New York both use daylight saving time, and on different dates. If your country doesn't, session opens shift in your local time.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/6/prompt: A trader only has time from 14:00 to 16:00 London time. Which plan makes the most sense?
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/6/option: EUR/USD during the overlap, checking US news times
A low-liquidity pair to get a tighter spread
Skipping the economic calendar since it's only two hours
Trading the Asian range breakout in these hours
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/6/explan: These two hours sit in the middle of the overlap, and EUR/USD is very liquid then. But US news (like 13:30 and 15:00 London time) lands here too, so checking the calendar is a must. Low liquidity means a wider spread, not a tighter one.
lessons/day-trading-u2-l3/steps/7/pairs/: Often starts the day's main move
The most liquid part of the day
